html:
The Battle of Hastings was fought on 14 October 1066 near Hastings in Sussex, on the south coast of England. Duke William of Normandy beat and killed King Harold Godwinson and won the English crown.

King Edward the Confessor died in January 1066 without children. Harold, the most powerful English earl, was crowned. William said the throne had been promised to him, and the king of Norway, Harald Hardrada, also claimed it. Harold beat the Norwegians at Stamford Bridge in the north on 25 September. Three days later William landed in the south. Harold marched back and took a position on a ridge, his men on foot behind a wall of shields. William had archers, infantry and mounted knights. The Normans could not break the line until some of the English ran downhill after knights who were retreating, or pretending to, and were cut off. Late in the day Harold was killed, perhaps by an arrow in the eye, and his army broke.

William was crowned on Christmas Day. In the Norman conquest that followed, a French-speaking nobility replaced the Anglo-Saxon one, and England was tied to France for centuries. The Bayeux Tapestry tells the story.
sum: The Battle of Hastings was fought on 14 October 1066 near Hastings in Sussex, on the south coast of England. Duke William of Normandy beat and killed King Harold Godwinson and won the English crown.
